title: Whole Rat Fixation Via Transcardial Perfusion
author: Kathleen Bai
materials: 300mL 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in 1X PBS (Use ~250-300mL of each reagent per rat) Tools:

Ensure you have proper tools and chemical reagents. Approximate volumes are listed, but may be adjusted based on rat size. Reagents: 1. 500 mL 1X phosphate buffered saline (PBS) 2. 300mL 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in 1X PBS (Use ~250-300mL of each reagent per rat) Tools: 1. Large surgical scissors 2. 3 Locking Forceps 3. Small surgical scissors 4. Rongeurs 5. Guillotine 6. Spatula 7. 50mL conical tube 8. Tape

steps.title: Prepare Perfusion Station
steps.instruction: Set up the perfusion station inside a fume hood with a grid and a covered waste bucket. Ensure large disposal tubing is secured to the table to prevent spillage.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 1X PBS and 4% PFA reagents in beakers, keeping them on wet ice (0-4°C).
Connect separate tubing from each reagent beaker to a Y-shape tubing shutoff valve.
Connect the third exit of the Y-valve to a tube with a secured 20G x 1in needle.
Thread the tubing through a peristaltic pump cassette and lock the cassette in place.

steps.title: Prime Perfusion Pump
steps.instruction: Prime the pump using the clockwise setting to remove all air bubbles from the tubing.

substeps.instruction: Set pump to 90 RPM for both 1X PBS and 4% PFA.
Verify consistent flow and lack of bubbles at the needle tip.

steps.title: Anesthetize Rat
steps.instruction: Place male and female rats in separate CO2 chambers and turn on the CO2.

substeps.instruction: Wait 3-5 minutes, observing until the rat takes its last breath and stops breathing.
Turn off CO2 and remove the rat from the chamber.

steps.title: Verify Anesthesia
steps.instruction: Perform a pedal reaction test by forcefully pinching the tip of the tail or hind paw.

substeps.instruction: If the rat reacts, return it to the CO2 chamber.

steps.title: Secure Rat for Perfusion
steps.instruction: Splay the rat's front and back limbs with the ventral side facing up and secure it to the perfusion grid using tape.

steps.title: Expose the Heart
steps.instruction: Make an incision to expose the abdominal cavity and thoracic cavity.

substeps.instruction: Cut horizontally above the genitals or in a 'V' shape, lifting skin with forceps to expose the abdominal cavity.
Identify the diaphragm superior to the liver and gently cut it to collapse the lungs.
Cut the ribs on both sides and clamp them out of the way for better heart access, ensuring lungs are not damaged.

steps.title: Cannulate the Heart
steps.instruction: Insert the 20 gauge catheter needle into the aorta, pointing towards the left atrium, and clamp the entrance.

substeps.instruction: Use forceps to hold the middle of the heart steady.
Avoid hitting the lungs or inserting the needle too deep to prevent leakage.

steps.title: Perform Perfusion
steps.instruction: Flush the system with PBS followed by PFA fixative.

substeps.instruction: Pump 1X PBS for 3 minutes at 90 RPM (~24mL/min) until the liver discolors from dark red to light brown (approx. 150mL per rat).
Cut the right atrium (dark red) and immediately turn on the PBS pump (alternatively, clamp the abdominal aorta to restrict flow to the brain).
Pump 4% PFA for 5 minutes at 90 RPM.
Reduce pump flow to 65 RPM and continue pumping 4% PFA for 15 minutes until the neck stiffens and liver pales (approx. 300mL per rat).
Perform a tail flick test to confirm fixation.

steps.title: Extract the Brain
steps.instruction: Remove the skull and extract the brain tissue.

substeps.instruction: Remove the rat from the grid and decapitate using surgical scissors or a guillotine.
Cut down the midline of the head under the skin and peel away skin to expose the skull.
Locate the foramen magnum in the occipital region.
Use rongeurs to chip away the skull in small segments from back to front, avoiding the brain tissue.
Once fully exposed, use a small spatula to turn the head upside-down and cut tethering nerves/connective tissues with surgical scissors.
Gently pull to remove the brain.

steps.title: Post-Fixation and Storage
steps.instruction: Fix and preserve the brain tissue.

substeps.instruction: Place the brain in a 50mL conical tube (volume should be 20x brain volume) filled with 4% PFA at 4°C for 24 hours.
Remove brain from 4% PFA after 24 hours.
Place brain in 30% sucrose solution (in 1x PBS) at 4°C for approximately 24-36 hours until it sinks to the bottom of the vial.
Store at 4°C until use.

steps.title: Long-term Storage
steps.instruction: If storing the brain for over 3 weeks, add sodium azide to prevent bacterial growth.

substeps.instruction: Use 0.02% w/v sodium azide in 1x PBS for whole brains.
Use 0.1% w/v sodium azide in 1x PBS for brain sections.
